findings.title: New recovery codes in user storage do not replace/remove existing local recovery credentials
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential treats a true return from user.credentialManager().updateCredential as success and returns without removing any pre-existing local recovery-authn-code credentials. If a federated user already has a local recovery-code credential, for example created earlier as a fallback, that credential remains in the local store and can still be validated. Newly generated codes therefore do not reliably revoke older codes.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is not removed
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated/user-storage recovery credential, but when allCodesUsed is true the code only calls removeStoredCredentialById. There is no corresponding disable/remove call for the user-storage credential. If the selected credential is federated, the exhausted credential can remain in the external storage and Keycloak can keep reporting the credential type as configured, leaving inconsistent state.

findings.title: Unsafe Optional.get can cause login page failure when recovery credential is missing or exhausted
findings.body: The bean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking presence. If the credential is absent, removed concurrently, or remains visible after all codes are used, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException instead of failing gracefully.

findings.title: User-storage test provider does not enforce single-use recovery codes
findings.body: isValid only checks whether the submitted recovery code is present in the stored list; it never marks the code as used or removes it. The added test also uses a code only once and does not attempt reuse or exhaustion. As a result, the new user-storage path is not validated for the required single-use behavior, and a replayable recovery-code storage would pass.

findings.title: Missing null checks on form fields can cause NPE
findings.body: processAction reads generatedAt and generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes from the form and immediately calls equals on generatedAtTimeString. A POST without one of those hidden fields causes a NullPointerException instead of redisplaying the challenge. Null-safe comparison or explicit null checks are needed.
